lessons.title: My family
lessons.canDo: Name the people in your family.
lessons.scenario: Smarty visits Mia and Sam at home. They show the people in their family.

items.note: We say ‘mother’ for the woman who is your parent; ‘mum’ is the short, friendly word.

image.describe: a smiling mother cat hugging a small kitten

items.note: We say ‘father’ for the man who is your parent; ‘dad’ is the short, friendly word.

image.describe: a proud father cat with a small kitten sitting on his shoulders

items.note: We say ‘brother’ for a boy in your family with the same parents; more than one is ‘brothers’.

image.describe: two young boy cats sharing one ball and laughing together

items.note: We say ‘sister’ for a girl in your family with the same parents; more than one is ‘sisters’.

image.describe: two young girl cats holding paws and smiling

items.note: We say ‘family’ for all the people who belong together at home.
Use ‘the’ before a person or thing when we both know which one.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a mother cat and her kitten. Which word fits the mother?
practice.explanation: The word for the woman who is your parent is mother.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Father is the man who is your parent. Listen to the last word.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about Sam.
practice.explanation: Sam is a boy, so he is my brother.

practice.prompt: Sam talks about his sister, Mia. Complete his sentence.
practice.explanation: Mia is a girl with the same parents, so she is my sister.

practice.prompt: Match each word with its other form: a short name, or more than one.
practice.explanation: Mum and dad are friendly short words. Add -s for more than one.

practice.prompt: Build a short sentence about the family.
practice.explanation: Both work: ‘the’ points to a family we know, and ‘my’ shows it is yours.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: You told Smarty about your family.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Mum is a short word for mother.

practice.prompt: Sam and Ben are boys. Complete: Sam and Ben are my ___.
practice.explanation: Two boys are brothers. Add -s for more than one.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen to the last word: sister.

story.hook: Who is in Mia and Sam’s family?

image.describe: The living room at Mia and Sam’s home: Smarty the black cat stands by a sofa while Mia, Sam and their mother and father smile and wave.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Hello, Smarty! This is my family.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: This is my mother and my father.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: I am happy. The family is happy!

questions.prompt: Mia says: This is my ___ and my father.
questions.explanation: Mia says: This is my mother and my father.

questions.prompt: Which word does Mia use for Sam?
questions.explanation: Mia says: Sam is my brother.

questions.prompt: Which word does Sam use for Mia?
questions.explanation: Sam says: Mia is my sister.

mission.setup: You are at Mia’s home. Smarty meets your family. Answer in your own words; an imaginary family is fine.

turns.smarty: Hello! This is my mother.
turns.hint: Say hello to Smarty’s mother.

turns.smarty: Is this your family?
turns.example: Yes, this is my mother and my father.
turns.hint: Say Yes and tell Smarty who is in your family.

turns.smarty: Goodbye, family!
turns.hint: Say goodbye to the family.

lessons.title: This is my…
lessons.scenario: Mia and Sam show Smarty their family, including a baby sister.

items.note: Use ‘his’ for something that belongs to a boy or man.
Use ‘her’ for something that belongs to a girl or woman.
Use ‘our’ when something belongs to you and another person together.
A baby is a very small child; more than one is ‘babies’.

image.describe: a tiny baby kitten sleeping in a basket with a soft blanket

items.note: We say ‘parents’ for a mother and a father together.

image.describe: a mother cat and a father cat standing close together and smiling

grammar.title: my, his, her, our
grammar.explanation: Choose the word by who owns it: my is for me, his is for a boy or man, her is for a girl or woman, and our is for me and another person.

practice.prompt: Smarty talks about Sam, a boy. You are not his sister. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use his for a boy: this is his mother.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Her is for a girl or woman. Listen to the middle word.

practice.prompt: Mia is a girl. Complete the sentence about her.
practice.explanation: Use her for a girl: this is her brother.

practice.prompt: You and Mia talk about your family together. Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Our shows that the family belongs to both of you.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a very small child. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: A baby is a very small child.

practice.prompt: Match the phrases with the same meaning.
practice.explanation: Parents means mother and father together.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Parents is for both mother and father.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: Mum and dad are our parents.
practice.answer: Mum and dad are our parents.
practice.explanation: Our parents means the parents of both of us.

practice.prompt: You and Mia are sisters. Talk about the mother you share. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: You share the mother, so use our.

practice.prompt: Lily is a girl. Complete the sentence about her.
practice.explanation: Use her for a girl: her name.

story.hook: Who is the baby in Mia and Sam’s family?

image.describe: Mia and Sam’s living room: Smarty the black cat meets Mia, Sam, their parents and a baby sister sleeping in a basket.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Mum and dad are our parents.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: She is happy. She is our baby!

questions.explanation: Sam says: Her name is Lily.

questions.prompt: Mia says: This is our baby ___.
questions.explanation: Mia says: This is our baby sister.

questions.prompt: Mum and dad are Sam and Mia’s ___.
questions.explanation: Sam says: Mum and dad are our parents.

mission.setup: You show Smarty a picture of your family. Answer in your own words; an imaginary family is fine.

turns.smarty: This is my mother. And you?
turns.hint: Tell Smarty about your mother or your father.

turns.smarty: My mother and father are my parents. Are your parents happy?
turns.hint: Say Yes or No, or say how your parents are.

turns.smarty: Say hello to our baby!
turns.hint: Say hello to the baby.

lessons.title: Who is she?
lessons.scenario: Ben visits Ana’s home and asks who people are.

items.example: Who is she? She is my sister.
items.note: Ask ‘Who is she?’ when you want to know who a girl or woman is.
Use ‘it’ for one thing or one small animal; ‘it’s’ is the short form of ‘it is’.
We say ‘grandmother’ for the mother of your mother or father; ‘grandma’ is the friendly word.

image.describe: a kind old grandmother cat with round glasses knitting while a kitten sits beside her

items.note: We say ‘grandfather’ for the father of your mother or father; ‘grandpa’ is the friendly word.

image.describe: a kind old grandfather cat with a walking stick reading a book to a kitten

practice.prompt: You see a girl and want to know her name or place in the family. Choose the question.
practice.explanation: Who is she? asks about a girl or woman.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Grandmother is the mother of a parent. She is for a woman.

practice.prompt: Build the question about a boy or man.
practice.explanation: Use he for a boy or man: Who is he?

practice.prompt: Ana talks about her grandfather. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: A grandfather is a man, so use he.

practice.prompt: Match each word to its other form.
practice.explanation: Grandma and grandpa are friendly short words. It’s is short for it is.

practice.prompt: Ana is a girl. Complete the sentence about her grandmother.
practice.explanation: Use her for a girl: her grandmother.

practice.prompt: Smarty asks: Is this your family? Answer with it, not with a person.
practice.explanation: Use it for one thing, like a family.

practice.prompt: Say the question aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: You asked who a girl or woman is.

practice.prompt: Choose the word for a mother and a father together.
practice.explanation: Parents means mother and father together.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Grandfather is the father of a parent.

story.hook: Who does Ben meet at Ana’s home?

image.describe: Ana’s living room: Ben and Smarty meet Ana, her grandmother and grandfather, who sit together on the sofa and smile.

questions.prompt: Ben asks: Who is she? Ana says: She is my ___.
questions.explanation: Ana says: She is my grandmother.
Ana says: He is my grandfather.

questions.prompt: Who asks the questions about the family?
questions.explanation: Ben says: Who is she? and Who is he?

mission.setup: You are at Ana’s home. Smarty points to people in the family. Greet them and ask who they are.

turns.smarty: This is my grandmother. Say hello.
turns.hint: Say hello to the grandmother.

turns.smarty: This is my grandfather.
turns.hint: Ask Smarty who he is. Use: Who is he?

turns.smarty: Is this a happy family?
turns.example: Yes, it is a happy family.
turns.hint: Say Yes and use it: it is a happy family.

lessons.title: How old are you?
lessons.scenario: Leo and Zara meet at Sam’s home and talk about how old they are.

items.note: Ask ‘How old are you?’ to find out someone’s age.
Say the number first, then ‘years old’.
Eleven is the number that comes after ten.
Twelve is the number that comes after eleven.

items.example: My brother is twenty years old.
items.note: Twenty is two tens, a bigger number.

practice.prompt: You want to know someone’s age. Choose the question.
practice.explanation: How old are you? asks about age; How are you? asks about feelings.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen to the number before years old.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about your age.
practice.explanation: Say I am, then the number, then years old.

practice.prompt: Omar is twenty. Complete the sentence about him.
practice.explanation: Omar is twenty, so the number is twenty.

practice.prompt: Match each number with its word.
practice.explanation: The number words match the numbers.

practice.prompt: Say the question aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: You asked about age.

practice.prompt: Smarty asks: How are you? Choose the best answer.
practice.explanation: How are you? asks how you feel. How old are you? asks your age.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for old in the middle.

practice.prompt: Leo says his age. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: My name is Leo. I ___ eleven years old.
practice.explanation: I goes with am.

practice.prompt: Which number is the biggest?
practice.explanation: Twenty is bigger than eleven and twelve.

story.hook: Who is the oldest person in this scene?

image.describe: Sam’s living room: Zara, Leo and Omar stand near the sofa and chat while Smarty the black cat listens.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Hi, Zara! I am Leo. How old are you?

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: I am twelve years old. And you?

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: This is my brother, Omar. He is twenty years old.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Hi, Leo! Nice to meet you.

questions.explanation: Zara says: I am twelve years old.
Leo says: I am eleven years old.
Zara says: He is twenty years old.

mission.setup: Smarty wants to know how old you and your family are. Use real or imaginary ages.

turns.smarty: Hi! I am Smarty. How old are you?
turns.hint: Say your age: I am … years old.

turns.smarty: How old is your brother?
turns.hint: Say his age. An imaginary brother is fine.

lessons.title: My friends
lessons.scenario: Sam, Ben, Ana and Lily talk about their best friends at Sam’s home.

items.note: Your ‘best friend’ is the friend you like the most.

image.describe: a black cat and another young cat giving each other a high five with sparkles around them

items.note: We say ‘boy’ for a young male person; more than one is ‘boys’.

image.describe: a young boy waving happily in a blue shirt

items.note: We say ‘girl’ for a young female person; more than one is ‘girls’.

image.describe: a young girl waving happily with a red hair bow

items.note: Use ‘they’ to talk about two or more people.
Say ‘they are’ for more than one person; ‘they’re’ is the short form.

practice.prompt: Which word is for Sam?
practice.explanation: Sam is a boy.

practice.prompt: Which word is for Ana?
practice.explanation: Ana is a girl.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: They is for more than one person. Listen to the last word.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about your friend.
practice.explanation: Best friend is the friend you like most.

practice.prompt: Sam and Ben are boys. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: More than one boy is boys.

practice.prompt: You talk about Ana and Lily, two girls. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Ana and Lily are girls. ___ are happy.
practice.explanation: Use they for two or more other people.

practice.prompt: Match each full form with its short form.
practice.explanation: Short forms mean the same as full forms.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: They are tells us about more than one person.

practice.prompt: Ana is Lily’s best ___.
practice.explanation: Ana is Lily’s best friend.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: This is Ben. He is my best friend.
practice.answer: This is Ben. He is my best friend.
options: This is Ben. He is my best friend.
This is Ana. She is my best friend.
This is Ben. He is my brother.
practice.explanation: He is for a boy, and best friend is the friend you like most.

image.describe: Sam’s living room: Sam and Ben sit on one sofa, Ana and Lily on another, and Smarty the black cat sits between them.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Hi, Smarty! This is Ben. He is my best friend.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Hi! Sam is my best friend, too.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Hello! I am Ana. This is Lily.

lines.speaker: Lily
lines.text: Hi! Ana is my best friend.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Sam and Ben are boys. We are girls.

questions.explanation: Sam says: This is Ben. He is my best friend.
Lily says: Ana is my best friend.

questions.prompt: Ana says: Sam and Ben are ___.
questions.explanation: Ana says: Sam and Ben are boys.

mission.setup: Smarty wants to hear about your best friend. Use a real or an imaginary friend.

turns.smarty: Ana is my best friend. And you?
turns.hint: Say the name of your best friend.

turns.smarty: Is your best friend a boy?
turns.hint: Say Yes or No, then say boy or girl.

lessons.title: Big and small
lessons.scenario: Smarty meets Leo’s family and Leo says how big, small, tall or short each person is.

items.note: Use ‘big’ for something that is large.

image.describe: a huge fluffy dog sitting next to Smarty the black cat who looks tiny

items.note: Use ‘small’ for something that is not big.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat gently holding a tiny kitten that looks very small

items.note: Use ‘tall’ for a person who is high from head to foot.

image.describe: a very tall boy standing next to a doorway, taller than the door

items.note: Use ‘short’ for a person who is not tall.

image.describe: a short girl standing on tiptoes beside a high shelf

items.note: Use ‘young’ for someone who has not lived long; it is the opposite of old.

grammar.title: Words that describe
grammar.explanation: Say who or what first, then the describing word: ‘Ben is tall.’ You can also put it before the person: ‘a tall boy’.

practice.prompt: An elephant is next to a mouse. Which word fits the elephant?
practice.explanation: An elephant is large, so it is big.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Small is the opposite of big.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about the father.
practice.explanation: A tall person is high from head to foot.

practice.prompt: Lily is not tall. Complete the sentence about her.
practice.explanation: Short is the opposite of tall.

practice.prompt: Match each word with its opposite.
practice.explanation: Opposites have the opposite meaning.

practice.prompt: Look at the baby. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: A baby is young and small.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: You described a person.

practice.prompt: Sam is tall and Ben is short. Choose the true sentence.
practice.explanation: Sam is tall, and Ben is short.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: She is for a girl. Small tells us her size.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about two boys.
practice.explanation: Put tall before boys.

story.hook: Who is big and who is small in Leo’s family?

image.describe: Leo’s living room: Leo shows Smarty his tall father, short mother, big brother Tom and a small baby sister in a cot.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: My father is tall. My mother is short.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Who is he? He is big!

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: He is my brother, Tom. He is a big boy.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: This is my baby sister. She is small and young.

questions.explanation: Leo says: My father is tall.
Leo says: He is my brother, Tom. He is a big boy.
Leo says: She is small and young.

mission.setup: Smarty wants to hear how your family looks. Use real or imaginary details.

turns.smarty: My father is tall. How is your father?
turns.hint: Say how your father is: tall, short, big or small.

turns.smarty: I am small. Are you tall?
turns.hint: Say Yes or No, then say tall or short.

lessons.title: I have a cat
lessons.scenario: Tom and Zara talk about the cat and the dog they have.

items.note: Say ‘I have’ to tell what you own or keep.
Say ‘you have’ to talk to the person you are speaking with.
A cat is a small animal; more than one is ‘cats’.

image.describe: a cute black cat sitting politely and looking at us

items.note: A dog is an animal that barks; more than one is ‘dogs’.

image.describe: a friendly brown dog wagging its tail

items.note: Use ‘an’ instead of ‘a’ before a word that starts with a vowel sound, like ‘old’.

practice.prompt: Which word is for Smarty, the black animal in the picture?
practice.explanation: Smarty is a cat.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen to the last word and to I have.

practice.prompt: Tell Smarty about your cat. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: I goes with have.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence for Zara.
practice.explanation: You have talks to the other person.

practice.prompt: Look at Zara. Choose what you say to Zara.
practice.explanation: To talk to Zara, say you have.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence about an old cat.
practice.explanation: Old starts with a vowel sound, so we say an.

practice.prompt: Match one with two.
practice.explanation: Add -s for more than one. Baby becomes babies.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: You told Smarty what you have.

practice.prompt: Tom’s dog is big. Choose the sentence.
practice.explanation: The dog is big, like the picture.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Baby sister is a small sister.

story.hook: Who has a dog and who has a cat?

image.describe: Tom’s living room: Tom and Zara sit on the floor, a big dog sleeps near Tom, and Smarty the black cat watches them.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hi, Zara! I have a dog.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Yes, it is big. And you? Do you have a dog?

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: No, I have a cat. It is small.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A cat! I have an old cat, too.

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: You have a dog and a cat!

questions.explanation: Zara says: No, I have a cat.
Tom says: Yes, it is big.
Tom says: I have an old cat, too.

mission.setup: Smarty asks about your pets. You can use real or imaginary pets.

turns.smarty: Hello! I have a cat. Do you have a cat?
turns.hint: Say Yes or No. You can say: I have a cat.

turns.smarty: Do you have a dog?
turns.hint: Say Yes or No about a dog.

lessons.title: She has a bird
lessons.scenario: Ben visits Lily’s house and they talk about pets.

items.note: Use ‘has’ with he, she or one name; use ‘have’ with I and you.
A house is a building where a family lives; more than one is ‘houses’.

image.describe: a cosy house with a red roof, a green door and a small garden

items.note: A pet is an animal you keep at home with your family.

image.describe: a girl hugging a small dog while a bird sits on her shoulder

items.note: A bird is a small animal that can fly; more than one is ‘birds’.

image.describe: a small blue bird singing on a branch

grammar.title: have and has
grammar.explanation: I and you take ‘have’. He, she and one person’s name take ‘has’.

practice.prompt: Which word is for the picture of a home with a red roof?
practice.explanation: A house is where a family lives.

practice.prompt: A cat, a dog or a bird at home is a ___.
practice.explanation: A pet is an animal you keep at home.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen to the size word.

practice.prompt: Tell Smarty about Lily. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: She goes with has.

practice.prompt: Tell Smarty about yourself. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: I goes with have, not has.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about Ben.
practice.explanation: A name goes with has.

practice.prompt: Match one with more than one.
practice.explanation: Add -s for more than one.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: You said what a person has.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen to I have and the size word.

practice.prompt: Mia has a cat. Choose the correct sentence.
practice.explanation: A name goes with has.

image.describe: Lily’s house: Ben and Smarty sit in the living room with Lily, a small blue bird in a cage near the window.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Hi, Lily! This is your house!

lines.speaker: Lily
lines.text: Yes! It is a big house.

lines.speaker: Lily
lines.text: Yes, I have a bird. It is small.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I have a dog. He is my pet.

questions.explanation: Lily says: Yes, I have a bird.
Lily says: My sister has a cat.
Ben says: I have a dog.

mission.setup: Smarty asks about your pets and your family’s pets. Use real or imaginary ones.

turns.smarty: Do you have a pet?
turns.hint: Say Yes or No, then tell Smarty your pet.

turns.smarty: My father has a dog. And your father?
turns.hint: Say what your father has. A real or imaginary pet is fine.

lessons.title: People I love
lessons.canDo: Say who you like and love.
lessons.scenario: Mia and Sam look at a photo of the people they love, and Smarty asks about them.

items.note: Say ‘I love’ for the people and pets you care about most.
Say ‘I like’ when you enjoy someone or something; it is softer than ‘love’.
A photo is a picture of people or things; more than one is ‘photos’.

image.describe: a girl holding up a framed family picture and smiling

items.note: Use ‘together’ when people are with each other, not alone.
Use ‘me’ when something is for you or done to you, like ‘say hello to me’.

practice.prompt: Choose the sentence that shows a very strong feeling for your mother.
practice.explanation: I love tells a strong feeling about someone.

practice.prompt: Tell Smarty about your cat. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Like and love both show feeling.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen to the last word: photo.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence for Smarty.
practice.explanation: Use me when you are the person who gets the hello.

practice.prompt: Mia and Sam are in the same room. Choose the sentence.
practice.explanation: Together means with each other.

practice.prompt: Match one with more than one.
practice.explanation: Add -s for more than one.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: You said who you love.

practice.prompt: Smarty asks: Who is she? Choose the best answer about Mia’s mother.
practice.explanation: Mia’s mother is a woman, so she is my mother.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence: Say hello to ___.
practice.explanation: Use me after to.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen to the last word.

image.describe: Mia’s living room: Mia holds a photo and shows Smarty, while Sam stands close behind them smiling.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: He is my father. I love my father.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: She is my mother. I love my mother.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Sam is my brother. I like Sam!

questions.explanation: Mia says: Smarty, I have a photo.
Mia says: I love my father.

questions.prompt: What does Mia say about Sam?
questions.explanation: Mia says: Sam is my brother. I like Sam!

mission.setup: You and Smarty talk about the people and pets you love. Use real or imaginary ones.

turns.smarty: I have a photo. I like my cat. And you?
turns.hint: Say what you like or love: I like my …

turns.smarty: Say hello to me! We are together.
turns.hint: Say hello to Smarty.

turns.smarty: Do you love your family?
turns.hint: Say Yes and tell Smarty you love your family.

lessons.title: Meet my family
lessons.scenario: Sam introduces his aunt, uncle and cousins to Smarty.

items.note: Your ‘aunt’ is the sister of your mother or father.

image.describe: a kind aunt cat in a pink scarf waving at a small kitten

items.note: Your ‘uncle’ is the brother of your mother or father.

image.describe: a cheerful uncle cat in a green hat lifting a small kitten

items.example: My cousin is twelve years old.
items.note: Your ‘cousin’ is the child of your aunt or uncle; more than one is ‘cousins’.

image.describe: two young cats of the same age laughing and sharing a toy

items.note: A ‘son’ is a boy who is the child of a parent.

image.describe: a mother cat with a smiling boy kitten on her lap

items.note: A ‘daughter’ is a girl who is the child of a parent.

image.describe: a father cat with a smiling girl kitten on his shoulders

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of Sam’s mother’s sister. Which word fits her?
practice.explanation: The sister of a parent is your aunt.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of Sam’s father’s brother. Which word fits him?
practice.explanation: The brother of a parent is your uncle.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen to the last word: cousin.

practice.prompt: My aunt’s child is a boy. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: A boy who is a child of a parent is a son.

practice.prompt: My uncle’s child is a girl. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: A girl who is a child of a parent is a daughter.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about a girl cousin.
practice.explanation: She is for a girl or woman.

practice.prompt: Match one with more than one.
practice.explanation: Add -s for more than one.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: You introduced someone.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.

practice.answer: He is my cousin. He is twelve years old.
